channel.title: Willis Strategy Group — Insights
channel.description: Articles and book reviews on leader development, experimentation, and capability by COL (Ret) Chris Willis.

item.title: Book Review: Cassino '44 — James Holland
item.description: Monte Cassino, Anzio, and the liberation of Rome — the brutal conclusion of the Italian Campaign trilogy, and its lessons for sustained large-scale combat operations.

item.title: Book Review: Dam Busters — James Holland
item.description: Operation Chastise as a case study in rapid capability development: from unproven concept to war-changing raid in under ten weeks — and the leadership that made it possible.

item.title: Book Review: Pacific Blitzkrieg — Sharon Tosi Lacey
item.description: How the Army and Marine Corps forged joint ground operations across five Central Pacific invasions — and why integration is forged by leaders, not declared by doctrine.

item.title: A Hybrid Approach to Combat Simulation Experimentation (I/ITSEC 2023)
item.description: Combining human-in-the-loop and closed-loop constructive simulation to capture both real-world applicability and statistical significance in warfighting experiments. By Willis, Bayer, Kelly and Anderson, Maneuver Battle Lab.

item.title: A Framework for the Accreditation of Simulation-Based Experiments (I/ITSEC 2021)
item.description: A cross-functional framework for accrediting the entire simulation-based experiment — models, scenario, environment, and analysis — not just the M&S. By Yanoschik and Willis, Maneuver Battle Lab.

item.title: Book Review: George Marshall: Defender of the Republic — David L. Roll
item.description: The Army's greatest soldier-statesman as a field manual for leader development: talent management as a weapon system, candor as a career strategy, selflessness as strategic capital.

item.title: Book Review: Project Maven — Katrina Manson
item.description: The story of the Maven Smart System, reviewed through a Battle Lab lens: what a decade of AI-warfare development teaches about experimentation, iteration, and fielding capability under friction.

item.title: Book Review: Sicily '43 — James Holland
item.description: Operation Husky and the first assault on Fortress Europe — timeless lessons on Joint Forcible Entry Operations, airborne fragility, and air and naval superiority.

item.title: Book Review: The Savage Storm — James Holland
item.description: Salerno and the battle for Italy, 1943 — what an infantry-centric slog against a determined defender teaches the modern student of large-scale combat operations.

item.title: Book Review: Brothers in Arms — James Holland
item.description: The Sherwood Rangers' transformation from horse cavalry to legendary tank regiment — and its lessons for the Army Transformation Initiative.
